newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bourse was due correction - Merrill analyst.
newsitem.headline: Greek bourse was due correction - Merrill analyst.

text.p: Greek shares, spooked into a freefall in the last two days by a capital market commission warning, had taken off too fast with the market getting ahead of itself, said Merrill Lynch analyst Mike Harris.
The analyst who had turned cautious on Greek equities said the market "just had to correct".
"My argument was that Greece was turning into a good three to five year story but the market was taking off too fast and getting ahead of itself," Harris told Reuters.
In a February 13 market report that went against most opinions, Harris had pointed out that the risk-reward profile of Greek shares was not very compelling.
"The market could give up about one third of its gains," Harris said. He saw limited upside potential for Greek equities when weighing forecast P/E levels versus estimated earnings per share.
"Consider also that the news wasn't really that new," he said, referring to reports of falling inflation and interest rates.

Although it didn't happen, this type of bull run would have seemed more natural right after the election, he added. This time around the rally was more driven by liquidity flows and less by the news factor.
Asked to comment on where stocks were headed now, the analyst said he saw no reason for the rally to be totally erased, despite the panic selling of the last two sessions.
"I don't see why the market should shed more than half of the rally," Harris said. "But when a correction turns into a panic situation, it doesn't really matter," he added.
Greek shares trimmed losses of over 6.0 percent on Friday to settle 4.65 percent lower at 1,303.63 points on the benchmark index. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
